description.value: An fMRI study of the neural correlates of a brief mindfulness instruction during expectation and perception of emotional pictures in healthy participants.

spans.text: To study the neural correlates of a short mindful state during expectation and perception of negative or potentially negative stimuli without a behavioral component, we used functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI)

value: we hypothesized that when expecting and perceiving negative or potentially negative pictures, mindfulness would be associated with increased activations in regulatory structures (DLPFC, DMPFC) and with decreased activations in regions associated with emotional arousal, such as amygdala and insula.

spans.text: We hypothesized that when expecting and perceiving negative or potentially negative pictures, mindfulness would be associated with increased activations in regulatory structures (DLPFC, DMPFC) and with decreased activations in regions associated with emotional arousal, such as amygdala and insula.

description.value: A pseudo-randomized parallel-group study comparing healthy participants given a brief mindfulness instruction with a basic group receiving no emotion-regulation strategy.

spans.text: we used functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) in a group of healthy subjects who were compared with a matched group not applying any emotion-regulation strategy
The groups were assigned pseudo-randomly (matched for age and gender).
Twenty-three subjects participated in the trial without any emotion-regulation strategy (‘basic group’), and 26 subjects were given a mindfulness instruction (‘mindfulness group’).

During fMRI scanning, the subjects performed an emotional expectation paradigm (described in detail in Herwig et al., 2007a , Figure 1 ), in which they expected and perceived cued emotional pictures of ‘known’ or ‘unknown’ valence.

description.value: Participants expected and perceived cued emotional pictures of known or unknown valence.

spans.text: the subjects performed an emotional expectation paradigm
The task comprised one run consisting of 56 randomized trials
The task was programmed with PresentationTM (Neurobehavioral Systems, USA) and presented via digital video goggles (Resonance Technologies, Northridge, CA).

instructions.value: The mindfulness group was instructed to be aware of the present moment without judging; the basic group was instructed to expect and perceive the emotional stimuli.

spans.text: The written instructions explicitly mentioned neither regulation/emotion regulation nor mindfulness but described common aspects of mindfulness definitions
